title: “The Redeemer Shall Come to Zion”

sparks.section: Fasting builds spiritual power and blesses people in need.

cards.text: Fasting can feel like just being hungry. Isaiah says the Lord had something way bigger in mind.
Is not this the fast that I have chosen? to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, and to let the oppressed go free, and that ye break every yoke?

The Lord's kind of fast isn't about looking holy. It's about lifting heavy loads, our own and other people's, and caring for people in need. Isaiah then lists the blessings that follow, like light, healing, and guidance.
Think back to a time fasting blessed you or someone else, and jot down one line about it.

sparks.reflectPrompt: If you fasted this month, what burden would you want it to help lift?

sparks.section: Honoring the Lord on the Sabbath brings joy.

cards.text: What if Sunday wasn't the day of "can't" but the best day of your week?

If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the Lord, honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words:
Isaiah invites us to call the Sabbath a delight. The shift is from doing our own thing to spending the day with the Lord, and that's where the joy shows up.
Pick one specific thing that could make next Sunday more of a delight for you.

sparks.reflectPrompt: When has a Sunday actually felt good to you? What made it that way?

sparks.section: Jesus Christ is my Savior and Redeemer.

cards.text: Jesus once stood up in His hometown synagogue and read this exact passage about Himself.

The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound;
Isaiah calls the Savior an intercessor, someone who steps in for us when we can't fix things alone. He heals broken hearts, sets captives free, and trades our ashes for beauty.
Make a quick list of a few ways Jesus Christ has blessed you or people you love.

sparks.reflectPrompt: Which line in this verse feels closest to what you need right now?

sparks.section: The Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light.

cards.text: Isaiah pictures a light so bright the sun and moon aren't even needed anymore.
The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory.
Isaiah uses light, darkness, and seeing to show how the gospel would bless the world in the last days. God is gathering His children out of the dark, and we get to help.
Read Isaiah 60:1–5 and notice every word about light or seeing.

sparks.reflectPrompt: Who in your life could use a little more light right now?

sparks.section: Christ will reign on earth during the Millennium.

cards.text: Imagine a day when the hard stuff you're carrying isn't even remembered.
For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind.
Isaiah saw the day Jesus Christ returns and reigns on the earth. Old troubles fade, and the whole picture is full of rejoicing.
Skim Isaiah 65:16–25 and count how many times Isaiah talks about joy or rejoicing.

sparks.reflectPrompt: What's one thing that makes you glad the Savior is coming again?
sparks.phrase: new heavens and a new earth

sparks.section: The Sabbath can be a delight to me.

cards.text: Tomorrow's Sunday. Here's your chance to plan it on purpose.

Then shalt thou delight thyself in the Lord; and I will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father: for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it.
Six days are for regular life, and one day is set apart. When we spend it delighting in the Lord, He promises to lift us up.
Make a little "box of Sabbath delights": write or draw a few ideas for tomorrow on slips and drop them in.

sparks.reflectPrompt: What's one small thing that would make tomorrow feel different from the rest of the week?

sparks.section: When Jesus comes again, He will bring peace and joy.

cards.text: Isaiah doesn't describe the future with dread. He describes it with joy.
But be ye glad and rejoice for ever in that which I create: for, behold, I create Jerusalem a rejoicing, and her people a joy.
When the Savior comes again, life on the earth will change for the better. Isaiah's picture is one of peace, safety, and people who are glad.
Tell someone one thing you look forward to when Jesus comes again, and one way you can get ready.

sparks.reflectPrompt: What would you most want to change about the world when He comes?

gameSparks: The Lord's fast lifts heavy burdens.
Fasting brings light, healing, and guidance.
The Savior gives beauty for ashes.
The Lord is an everlasting light.
When He comes, former troubles fade.
phraseMeaning: In Isaiah 61, the Savior comes to comfort people who mourn. He takes what feels burned out and ruined in our lives and gives back something beautiful.
